tasks.short: Advise and assist students in office hours, arrange appointments, and send follow-up links and materials.

steps.what: Biology lecturer advises and assists students in office hours
Student books an office-hour slot on the lecturer's booking page
Biology lecturer arranges office-hour appointments: by e-mail today; after the change students book a slot and the lecturer handles only changes and clashes
Biology lecturer sends follow-up links and materials to students

tasks.design: Students book office-hour slots themselves on the lecturer's booking page ({CALENDAR}), so appointments are not arranged by e-mail. Common follow-up material (practical guides, reading lists, past questions) sits on a course resource page that the lecturer links to. Advising students stays with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appointments were arranged by e-mail back and forth.
tasks.enabler_now: Calendars offer booking pages with set slots.
tasks.still_hard: Students in difficulty do not book slots.
tasks.human_edge: Encouraging a student who is about to drop biology.
tasks.altitude: Fewer e-mails about appointments; advising stays.

evidence.claim: Calendars offer booking pages with set slots.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student visit to the follow-up sent; formal study advice is outside.
Input contract: booking page published; fallback is e-mail.
Students book in less time than e-mailing; their booking is shown in s1b and priced there.
s2 keeps 30 for changes, clashes and students who still e-mail; s3 keeps 60 because the lecturer still picks the right material and writes a short note.

incremental.description: Biology lecturer keeps the resource page current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of the students still e-mail for appointments, so s2 keeps 65 (8.4); high: most book on the page as assumed (13.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search and screen the literature, run experiments, record lab data, analyse data and write the manuscript, format references, check the manuscript, and submit it.

steps.what: Biology lecturer searches and screens literature in the field of knowledge

loop.input: The research question and the library's citation databases.
loop.check: Each suggested title must resolve by DOI or catalogue, else it is dropped; the lecturer reads each abstract and keeps only titles that bear on the research question.
loop.stop: One search per question; if nothing resolves, the lecturer searches by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Topics are described in many ways; keyword search misses related work.

steps.what: Biology lecturer conducts research experiments in the lab
Biology lecturer records observations and readings during experiments: in a paper notebook today, in the electronic lab notebook after the change
Biology lecturer copies notebook data and instrument readings into spreadsheets; after the change instrument files import into the notebook and the lecturer checks each import
Biology lecturer analyses data and writes findings for professional journals
Biology lecturer formats references to the journal's style by hand
Biology lecturer checks the final manuscript: findings match the recorded data, and figures and references are right
Biology lecturer submits the manuscript to publish findings through the journal portal

tasks.design: A research search tool over the library's citation databases ({OTHER}) suggests related titles; any title that does not resolve by DOI or catalogue is dropped. Lab data go into an electronic lab notebook ({DATA_PLATFORM}) with instrument files imported, so data are not copied from paper into spreadsheets; the lecturer still records observations as before and checks each import. A reference manager formats citations in the journal's style. Experiments, analysis, writing and submitting stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Literature was searched by keyword, lab data copied from paper and references formatted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Citation databases suggest related work; electronic lab notebooks import instrument files.
tasks.still_hard: Field observations still start on paper.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which odd result is worth a new experiment.
tasks.altitude: The lecturer spends more time on experiments and writing.

evidence.claim: Scopus AI gives topic summaries and foundational papers.
Electronic lab notebooks can import instrument files.
Funder rules bar referees from using generative AI on proposals.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research question to the manuscript submitted; peer review is outside.
Input contract: notebook licensed by the university; fallback is paper.
The lecturer writes and submits every manuscript.

s1 keeps 70: suggestions replace some keyword searching, but screening stays. s3 is the first record of observations and keeps its full time; s3b keeps 20 for checking imported instrument files. s5 keeps 30 for checking formatted references.
research_questions: Do suggested titles add work the lecturer would have missed?

incremental.description: Biology lecturer updates notebook templates when an experiment type changes.

approvals.approved_version: The manuscript with text, figures and references exactly as checked by the lecturer in s6, submitted once to the journal through its portal; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the notebook does not import this lab's instrument files, so copying stays (s3b 100), and suggestions help little (s1 85) (5.2); high: imports and suggestions as assumed (13.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet colleagues on teaching and research issues, plan the meetings, write and share meeting notes, and co-write shared documents.

steps.what: Biology lecturer collaborates with colleagues in meetings on teaching and research issues
Colleagues mark their free times in the meeting poll
Biology lecturer plans meetings with colleagues: by e-mail rounds today, by a shared-calendar poll after the change
Biology lecturer writes meeting notes: typed afterwards today, edited from a consented transcription draft after the change

loop.input: The recorded meeting, when every participant consents.
loop.output: Draft notes with decisions and actions.
loop.check: Every action must name an owner who was in the meeting; the lecturer checks each decision and action against what was agreed and removes or corrects wrong ones.
loop.stop: One draft per meeting; if anyone declines recording, the lecturer writes the notes.
loop.why_not_simpler: Discussions are free-form; a form does not capture them.

steps.what: Biology lecturer checks the final notes: decisions and actions say what was agreed and each action has the right owner
Biology lecturer shares the checked notes with the participants
Biology lecturer co-writes documents by e-mailing versions to colleagues

tasks.design: Meetings are planned with a shared-calendar poll ({CALENDAR}) instead of e-mail rounds. When all participants consent, a transcription tool drafts notes with decisions and actions, and the lecturer edits them, checks each decision and action, and shares them once. Shared documents are written together in one online file ({DOCS}) instead of e-mailed versions. Discussing issues with colleagues stays with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Meetings were planned by e-mail, notes typed afterwards and versions mailed around.
tasks.enabler_now: Calendar polls, meeting transcription and shared editing are standard.
tasks.human_edge: Finding common ground between colleagues who disagree.
tasks.altitude: Less planning, note typing and merging; meetings stay.

reach.learn: Whether notes and documents are current.

evidence.claim: Meeting tools can transcribe recordings and draft notes; shared editing replaces mailed versions.
Systems able to monitor staff need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the shared issue to the document written; department decisions are outside.
Input contract: consent for recording; fallback is own notes.
Works council consent comes before recording.

Colleagues' poll answers (s1b) replace their e-mail replies. s3 keeps 50 for editing the draft; checking and sharing the notes keep their full time. s4 keeps 70 because only mailing and merging versions go.
research_questions: How much of the drafted notes is changed?

incremental.description: Biology lecturer asks consent for recording.

approvals.approved_version: The meeting notes with decisions and actions exactly as checked by the lecturer in s3b, shared once with the meeting's participants; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: participants do not consent to recording in half of the meetings, so s3 keeps 75 (15.8); high: recording in most meetings as assumed (19.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compare textbooks and lab equipment, check lab stock, fill the purchase request, check it, send it to purchasing, record the chosen textbook, and receive deliveries.

steps.what: Biology lecturer selects textbooks and laboratory equipment by comparing options
Biology lecturer checks lab stock of supplies by hand
Biology lecturer fills the purchase request to obtain materials and supplies
Biology lecturer checks the final purchase request: items, quantities, prices and budget code match the chosen items and the stock
Biology lecturer submits the checked request to purchasing: by e-mail today, by one submit in the purchasing system after the change
Biology lecturer records the chosen textbook in the course reading list
Biology lecturer receives and checks delivered equipment

tasks.design: Lab supplies are tracked in the lab inventory ({DATA_PLATFORM}) with barcodes, so stock is checked on screen. Items are picked from suppliers' punch-out catalogues in the purchasing system ({PROCUREMENT}), which builds the request; once checked, the lecturer submits it to purchasing in the system. The textbook is added to the course reading list tool from the library catalogue instead of typed. Choosing materials and checking deliveries stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock was checked by hand, requests typed and mailed, and reading lists typed.
tasks.enabler_now: Lab inventories, punch-out catalogues and reading list tools are standard.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the textbook that students will actually read.
tasks.altitude: The lecturer chooses instead of typing requests.

evidence.claim: Lab inventories with barcodes, punch-out catalogues and reading list tools are standard.

assumptions: Boundary: from the course need to the delivery checked; supplier contracts are outside.
Input contract: catalogues connected by purchasing; fallback is typed requests.

The lecturer checks every request. s2 keeps 50 for spot checks of shelves against the inventory; s3 keeps 40 for picking items and filling items without a catalogue; s5 keeps 20 for the submit; s6 keeps 50 for finding the edition and adding notes.
Purchasing handles system requests as it did e-mails.
research_questions: Do practicals start with all supplies more often?

incremental.description: Biology lecturer scans supplies into the lab inventory.

approvals.approved_version: The purchase request with items, quantities, prices and budget code exactly as checked by the lecturer in s4, submitted once to purchasing in the purchasing system; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: purchasing has not connected catalogues for most lab items, so requests are typed as today (15.5); high: catalogues connected as assumed (27.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The biology lecturer keeps advising, doing research, working with colleagues and choosing materials; e-mail scheduling, paper lab data, note typing and typed requests shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A lecturer with more time for research.
